n: Huntmaster of the Fells // Ravager of the Fells

faces.f: An enigma as vexing as life itself.
"We must save you from yourselves."
Moorlanders speak in awe of the priests' talent for arriving just in time to drive off the wicked things that prowl the ravished parish.
"Honorable tactics are for honorable foes. These werewolves are preying on innocent travelers. I'll stab them in the back while they sleep if I have to."
Avacyn's holy warriors kept hope alive in her darkest hours. Now they will carry that hope across Innistrad.
"We are Odric's sword. We strike without fear, for his mind has divined how our foe will be slain."
"The harder they try to extinguish my faith, the brighter it burns in the darkness."
In the town's final stand, they overcame the snarling beasts as well as months of insidious distrust.

"A boon from the angels should never be cast aside."
—Manfried Ulmach, Chief Inquisitor
"In these halls there is no pass or fail. Your true test comes with the first full moon."
Avacyn's most devout would forgo the Blessed Sleep to keep vigil.

"If you must go out at night, bring a mob."
—Master of the Elgaud Cathars
You don't want to see his trophy room.
The restless geists of common folk often continue their lifelong labors.
The remnants of Innistrad's corrupted angelic hosts collapsed to form the Flight of Nightmares.
"Salvation will not be granted by the Lunarch Council. It must be earned—at the edge of a sword, if necessary."
A spirit is both fettered and free—bound in some ways to its previous existence, yet able to transcend much of the corporeal.
Tamil had always wanted a closer look at a geist's lantern. Now he had an eternity to study one.
Only one vault was great enough to hold Emrakul.
His mind whirled with grand plans, never thinking of what might happen if he were to succeed.

"When you see a raven, head for the hills. It knows when the ghost-tide is headed in."
—Sved, fisherman of Nephalia

"Geralf's prowess continues to grow. He can now replicate my own creations with near-perfect accuracy."
—Ludevic's laboratory notes

"Dear brother, it's sweet that you have chosen to share your toys with Ludevic, but I too have found some new playmates."
—Ghoulcaller Gisa
The same magic that lets geists pass through our realm can force them out of it.
"Let's start fresh, shall we?"
"Either I know just the spell I need, or I'm about to."
"The ravings of the mad are laced with eldritch knowledge."

"Vanya Falkenrath's paintings are astonishing. How does she manage to achieve such rich crimson hues?"
—Stefan, art critic
Without a mind, it doesn't fear death. Without a soul, it doesn't mind killing.
Subservience to greater power is the only law in the pit.
It was a family reunion to die for.
"Soft dirt makes for light work."

"Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create."
—Liliana Vess

"Avacyn emerged from the broken Helvault, but her freedom came at a price—him."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar

"They won't be winning any beauty pageants, but they'll do the trick."
—Enslow, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
"If you're not surrounded by decadence, my question to you is—why not?"
Ancient evils dwell within the burning chasm called the Ashmouth, ever ready to devour those foolish enough to travel alone.
"Try again in the next life, darling."
On Innistrad, one person's windfall usually starts with another person lying face down in the mud.
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.
"You were so eager to take and consume. Yet when asked to give, you refuse?"

"Impressive."
—Chandra Nalaar
"One vampire for every family member I've lost."
"Some claim that rage is a cloud that obscures thought and vision. But I can assure you—I've never seen with greater clarity."
Mist is the geists' sorrow. Wind is their pain. Fire is their vengeance.
Spirits disturbed by ghoulcallers become geists driven by restless anger.
Gavony was their stage, and the moon their spotlight.
"Madness can't touch a mind ignited by genius."
"If you're not refining your tastes, what's the point of living forever?"
The chant was incomprehensible, but its power was unmistakable.
It uproots entire fengrafs to add to its twisted frame.
Emrakul does not grant wishes. Desires simply align to her will.
"I would fear this fight, bloodsucker, were I alone."
Animated by geists fused in its oak, it hungers for more life to add to its core.

"More rope may not be necessary."
—Kep, Lunarch inquisitor

"The cornfields promise a good yield this season."
—Radwick, farmer of Gatstaf
"You can face any danger when all of nature is on your side."
Visiting a shrine at the start of a journey makes the traveler more likely to finish it.
Otto the Hunter was filled with many grand ambitions. The snake was filled only with Otto.
The Ulvenwald makes no allowances for youth. Today's newborn is either tomorrow's hunter or tomorrow's lunch.
The surviving militia members reunited with their fallen comrades sooner than they'd hoped.
A soulless husk of endless hunger.
Better potent than predictable.
"We can go into the dark hand-in-hand or alone. I know which I prefer."
Great devotion yields great reward.

"Faith can quicken the stones themselves with life."
—Writings of Mikaeus

"Sturdy nails make for sound sleep."
—Cosper Lowe of the Silbern Guard
Meat is meat.

"Tomorrow wears yesterday's face."
—Kordel the Cryptic
It comes off as easily as your own skin.

"Ludevic saw it in a dream and set to work immediately, every detail already known. Can such genius be taught?"
—Stitcher Geralf
"The cathars have taught me many things, but I will never forget the hard, honest work that first callused my hands."

"Wings that once bore hope are now stained with blood. She is our guardian no longer."
—Grete, cathar apostate
"Even in our darkest times, Avacyn's light still guides us."
"You'll never believe what I heard."
Rumors are sparks: gather enough of them and something's going to catch fire.
She faced down a howlpack alone, saving her town at the cost of her life.
Since her passing, many more travelers have made it home alive.
Vampires from every bloodline mingled together, all swelling with pride to be seen at the event of the century.

"Metamorphosis is a process."
—Laboratory notes
The final pages of the experiment log were blank. Investigators found it abandoned on a desk in the researcher's lab, open, the pages flipping in the wind from a shattered window.
Serpents leave their eggs in the cold and inky depths...
...knowing their hatchlings are more fearsome than anything else that might come along.

"Unfortunately, all my test animals have died or escaped, so I shall be the final subject. I feel no fear. This is a momentous night."
—Laboratory notes, final entry
"There's no question that these waters are treacherous, but if there's one thing I've learned in all my years of sailing . . ."
". . . it's that the lure of the sea is impossible to ignore."
Rather than consort with demons, the Quietus Cult seeks wisdom from the dead.

n: Thing in the Ice // Awoken Horror

faces.f:
"It serves as evidence of the ancient power of the deep, a reminder that the sea is the only thing worthy of reverence."
—Runo Stromkirk
"Great Ormendahl, I kneel before you, a fragment of your will, a servant of your tyranny. I beg you, release the strength within me!"
Bones cracked, flesh split apart, and the screams of euphoric agony gave way to unholy laughter.
The cathars realized they had not tracked her—she had led them here.

"Never thought I'd see the day I'd be wishing to see just a plain old werewolf."
—Raf Gyel of the Quiver of Kessig

". . . heck, I'd settle for anything that even resembled a werewolf."
—Raf Gyel of the Quiver of Kessig
"I'm afraid it's bad news."
"My village's fear drove me into the wild . . ."
". . . and I will bring the fury of the wild back to my village."

"A werewolf's howl is terrifying, to be sure. But this . . . this was a chilling sound I somehow felt. I fear what will reply to it."
—Alena, trapper of Kessig

n: Huntmaster of the Fells // Ravager of the Fells
Chalice of Life // Chalice of Death

faces.f: The sweet taste of hope's promise.
The bitter taste of life's only certainty.

"I felt compelled to take the twisted stone, and I abandoned my horse's burden to accommodate its weight. Now, its continued glow illuminates my home and warms my mind."
—Garner Kroft, Moorland farmer

"There is a rich history in a blade like this."
—Old Rutstein

"Its previous owners had some stories to share, I'm certain."
—Old Rutstein
With Griselbrand gone, the Skirsdag eagerly awaited another demon to claim their devotion. Ormendahl did not make them wait long.
A golden helix streaked skyward from the Helvault. A thunderous explosion shattered the silver monolith and Avacyn emerged, free from her prison at last.
If it comes for you, die boldly or die swiftly—for die you will.
Its footsteps of today are the lakes of tomorrow.

"Its stones seem to serve a healing function, but removing them intact is an exhausting process."
—Tolarian research notes

"In times like these, people need to be reminded of compassion."
—Sisay
"Healing is a gift the divine ones have shared with us. It is a sacred trust."
The detailed dispatch could be summarized in four words: "Time is running out."
"I'm up here. You're down there. Now who's the lower life form?"
An angel's sword impales only the body; her righteousness penetrates the soul.
Capashen riders were stern and humorless even before their ancestral home was reduced to rubble.

The faithful will walk through streams of fire and emerge unscathed.
—Crimson acolyte creed
"My only dream is to destroy the nightmares of others."

"Serra's light isn't easily extinguished."
—Reya Dawnbringer

"We turned to see where the blow came from and saw only a distant light."
—Capashen lord

"The earth shook, the sky rained fire, and it seemed the world was ending."
—Benalish refugee

"At least they remember me."
—Gerrard

"Will history remember this as the day demons arrived or the day saviors arrived?"
—Barrin

"Not everyone gets a second chance."
—Hanna

The truthful will stand in the gaze of death and escape unharmed.
—Obsidian acolyte creed
Urza convinced many Dominarians not only to set aside their differences, but to embrace them.
No matter how righteous the cause, it helps to bring along some muscle.

"Do griffins fight to defend their homes or purely for sport?"
—Sisay

"Hanna would give up her own life before she'd abandon the *Weatherlight*."
—Sisay
As healers battled each plague, they learned more about the next.

"Everything is in place. Nothing can happen that isn't part of my plan."
—Urza
A beacon of hope for a battered army.
"It could be worse," said Gerrard, looking around. "Well, maybe not."

"Our victory must come from all of Dominaria, or it will not come."
—Urza
"Let my hope be your shield."
All Dominarians agreed on one thing: they would not go down without a fight.

"If I do nothing else, I will protect my people."
—Teferi
Its stature and stride increase with each step it takes.

"Strength in numbers? I think not."
—Gerrard

"I think he sees more than he lets on."
—Gerrard
Teferi wanted no part of Urza's battle plans, but both agreed the Phyrexian portal must be closed.
Gerrard savored a grim smile as the Phyrexian portals disappeared behind the *Weatherlight*.
Whether for good or ill, their arrival always means change.
"Above the waves you may be mighty indeed, but down here you belong to me."

"We define the boundaries of reality; they don't define us."
—Teferi

"I don't have time for you right now."
—Teferi

"Those who know only one path to victory can never hope to triumph."
—The Blind Seer

"Rise, metathran. You shall serve a nobler cause in death."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general
"We need alternatives, Hanna," yelled Gerrard. "Now!"
Children claim no two feathers are exactly the same color, then eagerly gather them for proof.
"You aren't invited."

"The subject's wings are clearly vestigial. We suspect the gems somehow keep it aloft."
—Tolarian research notes

"Wings are but fins for swimming the sky."
—Empress Galina

"This strange new beast makes for an excellent meal. Get me more."
—Empress Galina
"Let my wisdom give you wings."

"I suggest you take a closer look."
—Tidal visionary
Beneath the waves, things appear the way merfolk want them to.
Young tower drakes quickly learn to maneuver among Benalia's many spires.
"Deceit is the heart of war."
Not choosing sides in a war can be dangerous—but lucrative.

"Rest now. You've neither won nor lost, but this battle is over for you just the same."
—Teferi
"I knew this day would come," said Urza. Looking at the destruction, Barrin sighed, "You don't have to revel in it."

"I'll wring out your tiny mind like a sponge."
—Urborg witch

"Older specimens are completely encrusted with gems, which serve as both armor and weapons."
—Tolarian research notes

"Whatever Yawgmoth marks, dies. There is no escape."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general

"Urborg's magic is strong. Did Urza send you to protect us or to protect against us?"
—Urborg witch, to Barrin
Death's embrace need not be cold.
Once an angel, now an abomination.
Misery, filth, disease—all things that bring suffering to the world—only make Phyrexians more dangerous.
Serra's living warriors looked on in horror. "Where is our Lady now?" they cried.

"I'd strip away the world to see what's under it, but I'd never just leave it to these Phyrexian parasites and their false god."
—Urborg witch

Fouler than a necromancer's kiss.
—Jamuraan expression
In the dark, it's nearly invisible—until it exhales.
"Let my hate fuel your fury."
"They ride our trails as if they were designed to," said the guard. "They were," replied Gerrard.
Barrin waited for the nausea to pass or for Urza to say something else. He waited in vain.
After encountering them, Squee finally lost his appetite for bugs.

"It is Yawgmoth's will incarnate: an efficient machine that replaces inefficient flesh."
—Tsabo Tavoc
It desires only to help others shed the itchy wet skin of life.
Benalia was only the first nation victimized by Tsabo Tavoc's specialized killers.
Nothing is sacred to the rats. Everything is simply another meal.

"Death is such an exquisite sensation."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general
As Barrin exhumed his daughter's body, he finally realized the full price of his faith in Urza.
"The Phyrexians have progressed," admired Urza. "Their parts are interchangeable."
The cruelest strain of plague keeps its hosts alive long enough to return home and infect their families.

"No, *you* get the water. I ain't thirsty."
—Squee

"Their arrival marks the end of Yawgmoth's subtlety."
—Urza

Twilight falls. We rise.
—Necropolis inscription
A chilling fog with teeth of ice.
A writhing mass of rot, with sharp claws and a vicious spirit.
Those with the ability to change their nature survived Phyrexia's biological attacks. Everything else died.
"The invasion has awoken slumbering mountains," noted Urza. "Good. We can use all the help we can get."

"All my life I've fought these monsters. Today I finish that fight."
—Barrin
A skilled ranger can glance at the mud on your boots and tell where you last camped.

"Isn't he on our side?"
"Yep."
"Why's he spyin' on us?"
"Don't ask."
The spread of its hood eclipses all hope.
Kavu emerged all across Dominaria, but the first and the strongest came from Yavimaya.
The kavu evolved for centuries deep inside Dominaria, and some can draw from its strength.
Broken and punctured by dozens of Phyrexian portals, the angry sky began to spit lightning back at the world.
"Forget it. I'm not getting up today."
"Remember me?" Tahngarth roared. "Now I'll repay you for my stay on Rath!"
For his family, Barrin made a funeral pyre of Tolaria.
"Let my passion spur your victory."
"I know how this one feels," said Urza. "It's not like others of its kind and has been shunned for its differences."

"Its gems didn't stop pulsating until they were completely removed."
—Tolarian research notes
It's not eager to lose the *other* eye.

"This is a battle of pawns, for the highest stakes imaginable."
—Urza

"The blood of your ancestors ran heavy on this soil. Now it's your turn to sacrifice for the glory of Shiv."
—Viashino heretic
Fierce when roused, this breed of kavu is easily distracted by a strong voice or melodic tune.
Its slime liquefies the ground as efficiently as its fangs shred prey.

"They certainly are well protected. Too bad for them they're not well balanced."
—Sisay

"Think of the problems we'll face if you uproot entire continents," said Urza.
"I have," replied Teferi, "but the alternative is worse."

"Fire is the universal language."
—Jhoira, master artificer

"I can't imagine how anyone lives in Shiv, let alone why they choose to stay."
—Sisay

"They've returned for the mana rig, but it no longer belongs to them."
—Viashino bey
"All this time I thought Squee was useless," chuckled Sisay. "Who knew he'd be such a good shot?"
The power of the wild, concentrated in a single charge.

"The battlefield is cluttered enough. Be still."
—Multani, maro-sorcerer

"The mongoose blew out its candle and was asleep in bed before the room went dark."
—Llanowar fable

"For what are leaves but countless blades
To fight a countless foe on high."
—Skyshroud hymn
As Phyrexians descended, Multani paused to reflect on the beauty that might never be seen again.
No spot in nature is truly barren.

"It took magic to extract one of the stones and five people to carry it."
—Tolarian research notes

"They weren't part of my plan, but Gaea insisted."
—Urza
The appearance of the first kavu surprised Multani. As they continued to emerge, he no longer had any doubts about Yavimaya's ability to defend herself.
As a dark rain of Phyrexians fell from the sky, fountains of kavu erupted from the ground.
For the first time, elves welcomed Benalish soldiers into the forest with something other than arrows.
Llanowar rallied around Eladamri's banner and united in his name.
"Let my strength harden your resolve."
"The world calls and I answer."
"I've journeyed across Dominaria. Phyrexians are everywhere. Plague is everywhere. There's no place left to hide."

"Gaea's memory is eternal, and she exists in all things."
—Molimo, maro-sorcerer
All elvenkind stood against Phyrexia. The Quirion nation deployed its most spiritual adepts, who wielded the power of their native soil.
"All that matters is the path ahead."

"We hid such stockpiles all over Rath. We should continue that practice here."
—Lin Sivvi
"My army took centuries to gather," remarked Urza. "Yavimaya seems to conjure hers out of thin air."

"I have chosen my path. Who will walk it with me?"
—Eladamri
Under Yavimaya's peaceful facade beat the hearts of many savage beasts.
Gaea battles rampant death with abundant life.
The plagues robbed Dominaria of all but its dreams. Eladamri hoped dreams were enough.
Protected by druids for untold centuries, the forest began to return the favor.
The fruit of this fabled tree takes on the flavor of whatever food you love most.
In Yavimaya, flying low to join a battle can be a costly mistake.

"Dominaria touches us all."
—Molimo, maro-sorcerer
Llanowar forges weapons of steel. Yavimaya grows her weapons within.
"Your presumption is your downfall."

"If only an angel's wings could shelter us all."
—Barrin

"Don't laugh. It works."
—Yavimaya ranger

"From shards and splinters I call forth my living horde."
—Molimo, maro-sorcerer

"Life can be found in all things, even things unnatural."
—Multani, maro-sorcerer
Gaea forged her soldiers into self-wielding weapons that struck down all impurities.
Darigaaz decided his foe would be more useful as a weapon.

"Only vengeance matters now."
—Barrin
Her leadership forged the *Weatherlight*'s finest crew.
They stop for nothing, not even the end of a battle.

"You can build a perfect machine out of imperfect parts."
—Urza
"You think you can stop me?" hissed Tsabo. "I think I can kill you," replied Gerrard.

"Beneath her scars, Dominaria's beauty yet shines."
—Multani, maro-sorcerer
"Are they on our side?" asked Sisay. "If they kill Phyrexians they are," replied Gerrard.
"I never thought I'd spend my life fighting. I'm a maker, not a destroyer."

"You helped save my people from a Phyrexian fate. Did you think I wouldn't return the favor?"
—Eladamri, to Gerrard
"I think she wants us to eat it," said Squee, staring at the oily carcass the cheetah had dragged to their fire.
Dominarians gladly fought alongside kavu . . . until the kavu figured out some Dominarians were quite tasty.
Her armor and steed were borrowed, but her courage was hers alone.
The storm wasn't an omen. It was the fulfillment of one.
Unlike many hunters, these panthers have no need for camouflage. They're fast enough to catch any prey.
"Birds reach all parts of the world," said Barrin. "They will make excellent scouts."

"Breathe deep, Dominaria. Breathe deep and die."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general
It took Yavimaya a thousand years to breed them, but it took only seconds for them to prove their worth.

"How will you fight an enemy that cares nothing for itself?"
—The Blind Seer
Anything sent into a plagued world is bound to come back infected.
It sleeps with its claws open.
They sneer at the terrestrial dangers found on peaks and shores, eager to prove themselves against new and even mightier foes.
"I can preserve ten lives by taking one."
Barbarians long for a glorious death in battle. Phyrexia was eager to grant that wish.
Hot wind whipped up as if the weather itself wanted to fight Phyrexians.
It winds its way through undergrowth as easily as it swims through shallows.

"Isolation is not the answer."
—Urza, to Teferi
"I might almost pity my enemies—if it wasn't so amusing to watch them die."
"Which would you like first, the insult or the injury?"
Relentless as the sea, remorseless as death.
As battle raged in Shiv, a strange new ally appeared from below the ravaged ground.
The plague moved faster than an army and was far more deadly.

"Every last one of you will become my servant. It's a shame you won't live to see the irony."
—Tsabo Tavoc, Phyrexian general
There's no known antidote for the cobra's venom . . . or its appetite.
Urza knew Phyrexians would come through the air and sent his soldiers to greet them.
Not all elves embrace the pastoral life. Some still roam the forest's edge, forever making war against their hated enemies.
Kavu hunt prey in packs—one kavu hunts a pack of prey.

"We turned old weapons into new warriors."
—Jhoira, master artificer

"The stone whispers to me of dragon's fire and darkness. I wish I'd never pried it from the figurehead of that sunken Keldon longship."
—Isel, master carver

"Let insight and energy be your guides."
—The Blind Seer, to Gerrard
"Crosis is the eye of the ur-dragon, piercing illusion and darkness."
"Darigaaz is the breath of the ur-dragon, burning away the burdens of mortality."

"A strange skull was turned up by an Ephran farmer's plow. I traded a copper ring for the 'ox skull.' It resonates of the sea and danger."
—Isel, master carver
"Dromar is the wings of the ur-dragon, sweeping away all opposition."

"Those who can't survive are of no consequence."
—Tsabo Tavoc
Lotus fields are too valuable to leave undefended.

"Your life was meaningless, but your death will glorify Yawgmoth."
—Tsabo Tavoc

"There's nothing I wouldn't give to achieve victory. Can you say the same?"
—Tsabo Tavoc, to Gerrard
The sky split, and the air crackled and roiled. The Phyrexian invasion of Dominaria had finally begun.

"Great peril demands formidable weaponry."
—Urza
"Rith is the claw of the ur-dragon, scattering seeds of devastation."

"Today a seashell fell from the empty sky here in Kinymu, a hundred leagues from the sea. I'm torn—shall I carve a woman or a bird?"
—Isel, master carver
"Part drill sergeant, part training dummy," thought Gerrard. "I hope it can stand up to a real war."

"An elvish adventurer unearthed this stone in Jolrael's jungle. Now it's truly fit for display in one of her palaces."
—Isel, master carver
"Treva is the voice of the ur-dragon, demanding cries of worship."

"I found a troll-horn fragment in the wooded foothills of Hurloon, and it keeps growing larger. I wonder, is the horn recreating itself or the troll?"
—Isel, master carver
"It's a tool for aiding my other tools," explained Urza. "Now they'll work in harmony."
The Capashen built the highest towers in Benalia to afford themselves the best view.
Llanowar has seven elfhames, or kingdoms, each with its own ruler. Their palaces are objects of awe, wonder, and envy.

Only death breeds in stagnant water.
—Urborg saying
Only the hardiest explorers survive to eat the fruit.
Deep in the heart of Urborg lie massive volcanoes whose thick black smoke covers the land with perpetual darkness.

"The darkness crawls with vampires and ghouls, but we are not without allies."
—Mikaeus, the Lunarch
She endures without Avacyn but secretly asks each soul she guides if it has seen her.
From mortal hope immortal power springs.
Moorlanders speak in awe of the priests' talent for arriving just in time to drive off the wicked things that prowl the ravished parish.

"What cannot be destroyed will be bound."
—Oath of Avacyn
"I stand for every cobbler, tanner, and fool in this town—and they stand for me."
Death has bound it with chains of past regrets. Forever it searches for atonement, each kindness removing a single link.

"I heard her talking in her sleep—pleading, shrieking, snarling. It was not my daughter's voice. That is not my daughter."
—Ekatrin, elder of Hanweir
The fiend tormented them by recounting the girl's memories, as if some part of her remained inside that twisted shell.

"Never forget our ancestors. They have not forgotten us."
—Mikaeus, the Lunarch
Survival of the purest.
He vowed he would never rest until he reached his destination. He doesn't know how right he was.
"My greatest hope is that you will surpass me in every way, consigning my name to some forgotten corner of history."
"No matter how many I kill, there are always more to hunt. It makes me smile just to think about it."
People only say "I'm sure it was nothing" when they're sure it was something.
The spirit cares nothing for the crimes or triumphs of the slain. It shelters all beneath its stormy cloak.
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
"Ghoulcallers trying to get in, geists trying to get out . . . . This duty is never dull."
"In these halls there is no pass or fail. Your true test comes with the first full moon."
The path back to the world of the living is murky and bewildering. A geist may not even realize that it's terrifying its own loved ones.
"My faith is stronger than fang, claw, or mindless hunger."
"By the law of Avacyn, the following thoughts, words, and deeds are henceforth disallowed."

"Moonlight has a way of showing all things as they truly are—for better or for worse."
—Zilla of Lambholt
Some priests speak in whispers of the Helvault, a silver prison of unpurged evils.

"If you must go out at night, bring a mob."
—Master of the Elgaud Cathars

"No one chooses to be stitched together into a skaab. If it could speak, it would beg for its own destruction."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"If I fail to offer myself, we will surely be overrun. My fate would be the same."

"Be careful in your hunt. The clever little creature can steal your wards and lead you right into the werewolf's den."
—Britta, midwife of Gatstaf
You don't want to see his trophy room.
Though the old holy wards and roadside shrines have begun to fail, faith in Avacyn still holds true power.

"As long as we can utter a prayer or lift a weapon, we have the power to fight back."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
Never a word. Never a warning. Only the sound of hoofbeats along the crossways, and the screams of the avenged.

Let moss grow over gargoyles
—Gavony saying meaning "forget painful memories"

"I've learned to trust my dogs' instincts. When they're calm, I'm calm. And when they get nervous, I get my crossbow."
—Hinrik of House Cecani
"Looks like it's going to be a quiet night."
"The time for grief is over. The time for retribution has begun."

"Who says werewolves are the only ones who can hunt as a pack?"
—Kolman, elder of Gatstaf

"To show geists pity is to prolong their agonies. Whether they know it or not, they seek the Blessed Sleep, and we are to give it to them."
—Mikaeus, the Lunarch
"Priests, hunters, slayers—to arms! The enemy approaches!"

"I'd rather take on a neckbiter or moonhowler any day. Oh well, looks like I'm going to end up parrying with empty air half the night."
—Saint Trogen, the Slayer
Literally made for battle.
On Innistrad, death is just a career change.
Not content to nudge vases and chill drawing rooms, some geists muster spectral armies to claw at the hearts of the living.
"Me, angry? Of course not. Thanks to my research, I'm above such petty emotions now."
For a moment his basest desires run free, unshackled by reason or conscience.
Six feet of earth muffled his cries.
"Surely you know the joy of the hunt, my furry friend. My kind of hunt just takes a different form than yours."
After seeing his life's work drip away, the mage decided it was a good time to go crazy.

"Unfortunately, all my test animals have died or escaped, so I shall be the final subject. I feel no fear. This is a momentous night."
—Laboratory notes, final entry
"Garl, adjust the slurry dispensers. Garl, fetch more corpses. Garl, quit crying and give me your brain tissue. If he doesn't stop being so rude, I'm quitting."

"This abomination never belonged in our world. I'm merely setting it free."
—Dierk, geistmage
Unbreakable and unappetizing, the crab grows uninterrupted, sometimes to the size of a cottage and beyond.
Whether he actually exists is in question, but the terror she feels is excruciatingly real.

"The panic is amusing, but the real fun comes when the spell passes and the villagers start looking for a scapegoat."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist
"All that concerns me is the vampires' sense of smell and those freezing Nephalian nights."
His mind whirled with grand plans, never thinking of what might happen if he were to succeed.
Bound to the square where she died, she calls out to those in danger—usually scaring them straight into the peril she warns of.
The secrets she carried could have saved many lives, but they quietly drowned with her.
After several frustrating experiments, the visionary Ludevic realized he needed to create a monster that fed on torch-wielding mobs.

"It always amazes me what perfectly good things people throw away."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist
The heron is the symbol of the archangel Avacyn. The fact that such spirits still fly gives the church hope that its founder may one day return.
Even more than carrion, they crave the last words of the dying.

"Let those idiot priests tremble! A new era in unlife begins here and now. Oglor, raise the lightning vane!"
—Stitcher Geralf
"What some call obsession, I call the quest for perfection."
"The mist whispers to those who know it to be more than a mundane fog."
They call it "stitcher's anesthesia," a spell to deaden the senses while the mad doctors begin their grisly work.
The same magic that lets geists pass through our realm can force them out of it.

"Three heads, six arms, and some armor grafts are better than . . . the normal numbers of those things."
—Stitcher Geralf

"The church looks down on binding spirits into armor, but now I can look down on them."
—Dierk, geistmage

"The best skaab are more powerful and more beautiful than the sum of their parts."
—Stitcher Geralf
"Oglor create life, Oglor take it away. Oglor god! . . . until Master return."
"Either I know just the spell I need, or I'm about to."
Death took his humanity but not his skill with the knife.

"The demons don't care if we mutter niceties and act out ceremonies. Just kill him."
—Bishop Volpaig, servant of Griselbrand
Sometimes death comes knocking. Sometimes it tears down the walls.
He relishes the devotion of his Skirsdag puppets and their belief that it will earn them immortality.
It's not just the wind. It's not all in your head. And it's *definitely* something to worry about.
"May you and all your kin waste and wither until your clan is no more!"
The first step to peace is to learn how to forget.
The crueler vampires' idea of free-range farming.

"At least this one still has arms and legs. Well, most of its legs."
—Enslow, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
The demon Griselbrand dared to stand against Avacyn, earning him the loathing of thousands and the admiration of a few.
With Thraben's army recalled to its city walls, outlying villages were left to fend for themselves.
"I often think on how excited they must feel to be chosen as my prey."

"The living are born small and weak. The dead rise ready to serve. The choice is obvious."
—Gisa, ghoulcaller of Gavony

"Come. Bring your brothers. Tonight, you feast on living flesh."
—Jadar, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
She wanted to inspire terror wherever she went. The demons happily granted her wish.

"They won't be winning any beauty pageants, but they'll do the trick."
—Enslow, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
Lungs dried to parchment wheeze blasphemies within a cage of bleached bone.
Vampires of the Markov bloodline pride themselves on their exquisite taste in fashion, art, and "wine of the vein."
As the chapel was dragged under, the bell in the tower rang until the murky depths forever silenced its toll.
For a ghoul, every village is a buffet and every disaster is a reunion.

"Let go your grudges, or risk wandering the bogs forever in a murderous rage."
—Hildin, priest of Avacyn
Innistrad is a place where dreams invade the mind and mere shadows exact a terrible toll.
"Avacyn has deserted you. I welcome your devotion in her stead."
Its venom sacs are long gone, but its crushing strength is somehow greater than ever.
The bat has such clarity of hearing that simple sounds become symphonies.
Each form she takes is an exploration of the senses.

"And then I realized we all have skeletons on the inside. Why wait until the bodies are dead to control them?"
—Jadar, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
"Thraben's pleas fall on deaf ears. Ours do not."
"You'd best move along, human. Our palates are far less discerning than our master's."
Marella was delighted. The ball had attracted so many suitors for her daughter, including that handsome stranger. She wondered where the two were now . . . .
Kidnappers caught in Havengul are given two choices: languish in prison or become rat catchers. The smart ones go to prison.
All crave the Blessed Sleep. Few receive it.
He listens to every heartbeat, deciding which one of hundreds he will stop.

"Do not touch a drop. Not yet. I want to watch this so-called slayer's last crisis of faith."
—Olivia Voldaren
Some have endured the horrors of Innistrad by becoming the worst monsters of all.

"Is it hopeless? When wave upon wave of our dead return as mindless flesh-eaters to claw upon Thraben's walls? We're too busy cutting them down to indulge ourselves in such philosophical foppery."
—Mikaeus, the Lunarch
If there's anything a werewolf hates, it's a collar—especially Avacyn's Collar, the symbol of her church.
Its fiery paws make it easy to track, which is very useful when you want to go in exactly the opposite direction.
If it comes for you, die boldly or die swiftly—for die you will.

"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
While elder vampires select their meals with care, the newly sired frenzy at the first whiff.
Mist is the geists' sorrow. Wind is their pain. Fire is their vengeance.
"Do not flatter Fate. It did not guide you into my clutches tonight. That was all my doing."

"Innocent thorns can fill the air with your bloodscent. Don't stray from the path."
—Elmut, crossway watcher
When the moon rises and the bloodlust takes hold, nothing matters but the kill.

"May your veins weep, and may every vampire take notice."
—Stensian curse
Her mind was quite gone, yet she spoke nothing but truth.
A devil's hands are never idle.
No slinking in the dark for them, no luring whispers. They claim their prey in the speed and glory of the hunt.

"The wolves no longer hunt just to feed. They kill for sport, or for some madness behind their eyes."
—Elmut, crossway watcher
Those who only believe themselves infected with lycanthropy can be as dangerous as those who really are.
Innistrad pyromancers find their best raw materials in the fury of the dead.
He scans for wolves, knowing there's one he can never anticipate.
Technically he never left his post. He looks after the wolf wherever it goes.
Corpses destroyed by fire form the most destructive geists.
"Oh mighty Griselbrand, Scourge of the Heedless World, gladly I consume myself for thee!"
Few entrances lead to where demons and devils lurk. Unfortunately, they occasionally open new ones.

"Don't be afraid when you hear the wolves howl. Be afraid when you don't hear them at all."
—Saint Trogen, the Slayer

n: Kruin Outlaw // Terror of Kruin Pass

faces.f: "Hold tight. I've got a surprise for them."
Vampires think of themselves as the indisputable nobility of Innistrad, able to do as they please. There are few who can prove them wrong.
Shiny polished silver can ward off many creatures, but it attracts others.
The ingenuity of goblins, the depravity of demons, and the smarts of sheep.
"Some lament these haunted times, but I'm a geistflame-tank-half-full kind of person."
"If you're not having fun, what's the point of living forever?"
"Yes, I'm alone. No, I'm not worried."
Before she just wanted to snatch your purse; now she'll take the whole arm.
Devils are demons' unearthly desires made flesh. Let loose on the world, they satisfy their mad craving for destruction in a whirlwind of chaos.
When demons open a path to your front door, it's time to move.
Stensian villagers mourned the loss of human life. Thraben vampire slayers mourned the loss of living wood.
"Within blood is life. Within life is fire. Within fire is the path to our masters' glory!"
"A responsible king walks among his subjects."
"Hey lads, the moon's rising. All the better to watch him beg for mercy."
"Just look at him, groveling on all fours! What a pathetic—uh-oh."

"I can make you dance to my tune like a puppet, your very blood eager to obey."
—Olivia Voldaren
Many peasants secretly admire vampires' glamour and elegance—until they witness a moment of pure bloodlust.
Each night, he abandons the trappings of civilization.
Each morning, he repairs the front door.

"Living creatures seldom impress me. But I like this one."
—Uta Falkenrath
"Avacyn's protection is everywhere. From the holy church to the sacred glade, all that we see is under her blessed watch."
The only thing it likes more than discovering a pit of bones is adding to it.

"Civilization is fertilizer."
—Garruk Wildspeaker
Werewolf slayers don't know for certain how werewolves are created. So they kill all the wolves, just to be safe.
Hopes and prayers can carry the same force as swords and torches.
Wander too far into the wild and it may take you for its own.

"Bury your dead deep. The boars are hungriest while the corpse is still warm."
—Paulin, trapper of Somberwald
Some lycanthropes wish they could abandon their weak human shapes and revel in the power of the wolf.

"What is worse than a wolf in sheep's clothing?"
—Wolfhunter's riddle
Nature abhors a zombie.
Seen as unsavory, the hunters were never allowed in town—until one night they vanished.
The boot prints became paw prints, and they led right back into town.
"I would fear this fight, bloodsucker, were I alone."
After werewolves slaughtered the citizenry of Hollowhenge, other creatures moved in.
"They put bars on these noble beasts and then wonder why werewolves target our towns."
In the forest villages of Kessig, parents feed their children wormwood and other bitter herbs, hoping to make them less palatable to things that roam the night.
Animated by geists fused in its oak, it hungers for more life to add to its core.
In Gavony wishing is taken as a sign of weakness, yet the wells usually brim with silver.
He can deny his true nature for only so long.
The border between life and death is as thin as a layer of topsoil.
The land knows no difference between the graves of commoners and nobles.

"Stone and thought fade into ruin. Only the wind in the leaves will endure."
—Tomb inscription

"Pick not the rotten fruit, but neither touch the best. Leave those as an offering for our unseen guests."
—Radwick, farmer of Gatstaf

"There will come a time when the only prey left will be each other."
—Ulrich of Krallenhorde Pack

"You don't find many old werewolf hunters."
—Paulin, trapper of Somberwald
In the remote corners of Kessig, protection is found in secret powers unknown to the Church of Avacyn.
Stensian vampires encourage spiders near their manors so they can rob the webs.

"Nobody's seen the Lady of Videns for years. Poor dear, no companions at all in that old castle."
—Yonda of Gavony
Visiting a shrine at the start of a journey makes the traveler more likely to finish it.
The executioner's tree in Thraben Cathedral holds the power to absolve more than the souls of the hanged.
"With this ritual, we cast aside our fragile humanity . . ."
". . . and embrace the ancient ferocity of the undying Wild."

n: Villagers of Estwald // Howlpack of Estwald

faces.f: You can spot a werewolf-infested town by its lack of butcher shops.
Estwald's citizens don't dislike outsiders—they taste just fine.
"Whatever did this is near. Death reversion has not yet occurred. Be alert!"
Before you travel the woods of Kessig, first get permission from those who died trying.
You can always tell the evil one by the dagger he's sticking in you.
Outside the safety of Thraben, there is little distinction between tool and weapon.
As if anyone needed another reason to avoid dark, dank cellars.
For the necro-alchemist, any puzzle can be solved with intelligence and harvested body parts.
A child's porcelain doll went missing one night, as did a pair of kitchen shears and the town magistrate.
It comes off as easily as your own skin.
The rigs were outlawed except in Nephalia, where malign spirits are as plentiful as crazed inventors.
The bell's chime heralds the rise of the unhallowed from the grave and the fall of their victims into the earth.
Thanks to Havengul's thriving illegal market for corpses, the shovel that interred a body during the day is usually the same one digging it out at night.
Nothing could break it but the fall.
It hides the face and protects the soul.
Farmhands and priests mutter curses at the ragged thing; it unnerves more than just the crows.
As sharp as its bearer's words of faith.
Not everyone can have a sword of blessed silver. Not everyone needs one, either.
Magical etchings turned a whittler's tool into a wolfhunter's weapon.
The rider set off into the eerie mist, swaddled in armor and laden with amulets.
Where cathars learn to fight not only demons and vampires, but ignorance as well.

"The protective wards of the church have weakened, and no one can tell us why. It's time to look to our own defenses."
—Gregel, militia leader
Deserted, but not uninhabited.
In places where the sea meets the trees, it's easy to forget the darkness that rules most of Innistrad.
Not every church is a place of faith.
When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.

"Some see a coastal disaster. I see a fully-stocked seagraf."
—Jadar, ghoulcaller of Nephalia

"This is the price of being last in the food chain. We must keep our places of beauty hidden away instead of displayed for all to see."
—Hildin, priest of Avacyn
The revelry ends when the supply of fresh ingenues runs dry.
Skirsdag cultists meet behind a waterfall's curtain and plot with demonic forces.
Farmers cut the trees and buried their dead. The dead rose up and killed the farmers. The trees grew back and strangled the dead.

"Healing is a matter of time, but it is sometimes also a matter of opportunity."
—D'Avenant proverb

Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the Mesa Pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a Mesa Pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.

"'Do you know, I always thought Unicorns were fabulous monsters, too? I never saw one alive before!' 'Well, now that we *have* seen each other,' said the Unicorn, 'if you'll believe in me, I'll believe in you.'"
—Lewis Carroll

Most human scholars believe that Merfolk are the survivors of sunken Atlantis, humans adapted to the water. Merfolk, however, believe that humans sprang forth from Merfolk who adapted themselves in order to explore their last frontier.

"While, like a ghastly rapid river,
Through the pale door,
A hideous throng rush out forever,
And laugh—but smile no more."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"
Although greatly prized among falconers, the Zephyr Falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.
On guard for larger dangers, we underestimated the power and speed of the Imp's muck-crusted claws.
'Twas in the bogs of Cannelbrae My mate did meet an early grave 'Twas nothing left for us to save In the peat-filled bogs of Cannelbrae.

Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—
But those who go with her are never the same.
When Raganorn unsealed the catacombs, he found more than the dead and their treasures.

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose,
Nor spake, nor moved their eyes;
It had been strange, even in a dream,
To have seen those dead men rise."
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"

"For something is amiss or out of place When mice with wings can wear a human face."
—Theodore Roethke, "The Bat"
The Wall of Bone is said to be an aspect of the Great Wall in Hel, where the bones of all sinners wait for Ragnarok, when Hela will call them forth for the final battle.
Fortunately, Hill Giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.
Generations of genetic weeding have given rise to the deviously cowardly Ironclaw clan. To say that Orcs in general are vicious, depraved, and ignoble does not do justice to the Ironclaw.

The intricate dynamics of Rundvelt Goblin affairs are often confused with anarchy. The chaos, however, is the chaos of a thundercloud, and direction will sporadically and violently appear. Pashalik Mons and his Raiders are the thunderhead that leads in the storm.
In a rare display of ingenuity, the Orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most Orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.

"Hi! ni! ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me! Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return."
—Navajo war chant

"And the unclean spirits went out, and entered the swine: and the herd ran violently . . . ."
—Mark 5:13

"Sometimes it is better to be swift of foot than strong of swordarm."
—Elven proverb
I tell you, there was so many arrows flying about you couldn't hardly see the sun. So I says to young Angus, "Well, at least now we're fighting in the shade!"

Don't try to outrun one of Dominia's Grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.
The only sound was the gentle clicking of the Faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the Scryb were very funny anymore.
I didn't think Mammoths could ever hold a candle to a well-trained battle horse. Then one day I turned my back on a drunken soldier. His blow never landed; Mi'cha flung the brute over ten meters.

"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!"
—William Shakespeare, King Lear
By the time Mishra was defeated, no mage was foolish enough to rely heavily on walls.
